cards.front: Translate: attendre.
Translate: actuellement.
Translate: une librairie.
Translate: demain.
Translate: hier.
Translate: pourtant.
Translate: assez.
Translate: rarement.
Translate: la vie privée.
Translate: un emploi.
Write seventy in French.
Write eighty-one in French.
Give two possible meanings of le temps.
Give two possible meanings of une histoire.
Explain the difference between ou and où.
back: Où means **where**; the accent changes the meaning.

cards.front: Translate: Je n'aime plus ce film.
back: I no longer like this film.
Plus with ne means no longer, not more here.

cards.front: Translate: Il est huit heures et demie.
Translate: neuf heures moins le quart.
Read: Le billet coûte quinze euros, mais demain il coûtera treize euros. Give today's and tomorrow's prices.
Give the English meaning of rapidement and identify its base adjective.
Translate: J'ai besoin de temps.
back: Learn **avoir besoin de** as a phrase.

cards.front: What is the difference between une journée and un voyage?
back: Une journée is a day as a duration; un voyage is a journey or trip.

cards.front: Translate into French: I take the bus because it is useful.
back: Je prends le bus parce que c'est utile.
Prends is an irregular form of prendre.

cards.front: Translate into French: Yesterday, I sent a message to my friend.
back: Hier, j'ai envoyé un message à mon ami / amie.
Use the perfect for yesterday's finished action.

cards.front: Translate: Normalement, je lis, mais aujourd'hui je préfère sortir.
back: Normally, I read, but today I prefer to go out.
Keep the contrast and the two different activities.

cards.front: Explain how impossible, préparation and deuxième relate to their base words.
Translate: J'attends mon ami devant la librairie. Ensuite, nous allons à la bibliothèque parce qu'il faut préparer nos examens.
back: I am waiting for my friend outside/in front of the bookshop. Then we are going to the library because we need to prepare for our exams.
Attends means wait, librairie means bookshop, bibliothèque means library, and il faut expresses necessity.

cards.front: Translate into French: My room is small, but it is quiet. Tomorrow, I am going to study there with my friends.
back: Ma chambre est petite, mais elle est calme. Demain, je vais y étudier avec mes amis.
Chambre is feminine; petite agrees; elle refers to the room; y means there and precedes étudier.

cards.front: Translate: I have not finished yet.
How do “déjà” and “pas encore” differ?
back: Déjà means already. Pas encore means not yet.

cards.front: Translate: There is too much noise.
back: Il y a trop de bruit.

cards.front: Choose meilleur or mieux: She plays better.
Choose meilleur or mieux: This film is better.
What three checks help when inferring a derived word?
back: Use its familiar base, grammatical role and the meaning of the complete sentence.

cards.front: Translate both: une librairie; une bibliothèque.
back: Une librairie is a bookshop. Une bibliothèque is a library.

cards.front: Why should ou and où be learned separately?
back: Ou means or. Où means where. The accent changes the word’s function and meaning.

cards.front: Translate: I never play on Mondays.
back: Je ne joue jamais le lundi.

cards.front: Write 71, 80 and 81 in standard French.
Translate: fifteen euros fifty.
What time is “neuf heures moins le quart”?
Why learn a noun with its article?
back: The article records its gender and supports later adjective and pronoun choices.

cards.front: Why practise producing French as well as recognising it?
back: Recognition alone may not provide the spelling and form needed to write or say the word independently.
